archetype.name: Gunslinger (vertical)
archetype.definition: A rhythm-and-play-action passer who wins by pushing the ball 10-plus yards downfield and accepts a high interception rate as the cost of that aggression.

report.headline: The deep ball still works; everything short of the sticks has collapsed.
report.take:
Darnold has spent two seasons as one of the league's more efficient passers: 8.49 yards per attempt and a +5.2 CPOE last year, after a 2024 that ranked inside the top ten in most categories. The same career log also shows a quarterback who has thrown a lot of interceptions everywhere he has been, 61st of 63 in picks last season. Seattle built around both sides of that. This year the downside has stayed and much of the efficiency has gone. He sits at -0.072 EPA per dropback (32nd of 49) with a 4.3% interception rate (43rd), and his CPOE is down 7.2 points from last season.

Split his throws by depth and the season looks like two different quarterbacks. On balls 10-plus air yards he is at +0.453 EPA per attempt and +30.3 in total, and the 20-plus bucket is outstanding: +1.114 per attempt with a +15.3 CPOE on 20 throws. Under 10 yards he is at -0.177 per attempt, -25.1 in total, with a -5.5 CPOE. Throws behind the line alone cost -18.9. The quick game is supposed to cover for a struggling line and a 28th-ranked run game. Here it is failing, through screens that go nowhere and short misses. His top two non-JSN targets, AJ Barner and Rashid Shaheed, are both deep in negative EPA per target.

The line explains a lot of this. He has been pressured on 30.7% of dropbacks, 41st of 42, and the offense's hit rate ranks 28th. Pressure shows up most on third down (-0.301 EPA, a 30.6% conversion rate at 8.3 yards to go) and in one-score games (-31.6 total EPA). The 2.99-second time to throw and the 18.66% aggressiveness, up from 13.2, suggest he is holding the ball and forcing tight windows rather than taking the underneath answer. That is partly a quarterback trying to make up for a run game that does nothing. When he got clean pockets, as against Kansas City (6.7% pressured, +12.2 EPA), he looked like last year's player.

Now he is out with a quadriceps injury, with an estimated return of November 29. The two starters protecting him, Quenton Nelson and Charles Cross, are also out, though both carry earlier return estimates. The question for the rest of his season is whether he comes back to a healthy line. If he does, the deep game and Jaxon Smith-Njigba give him a real floor. If he doesn't, expect more of the same volatile results.

strengths.title: Vertical passing remains top-shelf
strengths.body: His 20-plus air-yard throws are producing more than a point of EPA each, with completion well over expectation. His intermediate work is also solidly positive. This matches last year's profile, which was built on downfield efficiency, so the skill is real. The 20-attempt deep sample will regress somewhat, but the 10-plus group as a whole is a large enough sample to trust.

strengths.title: Smith-Njigba connection carries the offense
strengths.body: Smith-Njigba has drawn 68 targets at +0.585 EPA per target, more total EPA than the entire passing game has produced. That is a sustainable alpha relationship, not a hot streak. As long as JSN is on the field, Darnold has a dependable way to beat coverage when the line holds.

strengths.title: Scrambles and ball security
strengths.body: His nine scrambles have averaged over a point of EPA, and six of them moved the chains. He has lost no fumbles despite heavy pressure. The scrambles are a small but useful escape valve behind this line.

concerns.title: Short game and screens bleeding points
concerns.body: Throws under 10 air yards, the majority of his attempts, are well below average in both accuracy and EPA. Throws behind the line are a disaster. Some of that comes from blocking and the receivers involved: Barner and Shaheed are both deeply negative. But a -6.2 CPOE on short throws is also on the quarterback. It is the biggest break from his 2024-25 form and the thing most likely to improve if the line stabilizes.

concerns.title: Interceptions above even his norm
concerns.body: A 4.3% interception rate puts him on a 22-interception pace. He has always thrown picks, but the rise in aggressiveness this year has pushed it higher. Expect some regression toward his career rate, not a cure: turnovers come with his style.

concerns.title: Pressure and the offensive line
concerns.body: He has been pressured more often than nearly any qualifier, and the team's hit rate allowed ranks near the bottom. That pressure shows up in third-down and one-score results. With Nelson and Cross both out as of the latest report, this is the variable that decides his return.

trend.note: Game EPA has swung from +4.1 at Washington to -12 against San Francisco, then +12.2 against Kansas City and -6.5 against Chicago. Clean pockets produce his good games; pressure games go sideways, and his last outing came with a 32.4% bad-throw rate.

nextGame.headline: Ruled out; a soft Raiders pass defense goes to Drew Lock
nextGame.body:
On paper this is exactly the matchup Darnold needs. Las Vegas ranks 28th in pass EPA allowed and dead last in EPA allowed on short throws. It also allows the most passing touchdowns per game to quarterbacks. The quick game that has failed him all year would have had its easiest test of the season.

It doesn't matter for him this week. He is listed Out with a quadriceps injury, and his return estimate is November 29. Drew Lock, questionable with an oblique strain the coach says he can manage, would start behind a line missing Nelson and Cross. For Darnold, the real takeaway is whether those two linemen are back by the time he is.

keyMatchups.title: Raiders can't stop the short game
keyMatchups.body: Las Vegas is the worst defense in the league against short passes and 31st in success rate allowed. That is the weak spot of Darnold's season. It is a useful test of whether Seattle's underneath problems come from the scheme or from the quarterback, even with Lock taking the snaps.

keyMatchups.title: JSN against a stingy WR1 profile
keyMatchups.body: The Raiders have held opposing top receivers under their usual output, while getting hit hard by WR2s. That points the opportunity toward Seattle's secondary options, which is exactly where this passing game has been weakest.

keyMatchups.title: Seattle line missing both anchors
keyMatchups.body: Cross and Nelson have played nearly every snap this season, and both are out. Las Vegas gets home pressure at a decent rate, eighth in hit rate. Whoever starts at quarterback will be working behind backups.

nextGame.watch: Whether Nelson and Cross return on schedule. Darnold's outlook depends more on his protection than on his quad.

restOfSeason.body:
Assuming he returns around the November 29 estimate, expect something between this season's numbers and last year's, not a return to 2025. The vertical efficiency and the JSN connection are durable. The short-game CPOE collapse should ease if the line is whole, because much of it traces to pressure, and the defense (fifth in EPA, first against the deep ball) should keep game scripts manageable. The interception rate should come down from 4.3% but will stay above league average, since that has been true of him every year.

Seattle runs well below its expected pass rate, so volume caps the yardage. A healthy version is roughly a 215-250 yard passer with a little over a touchdown a game and an interception most weeks. If the line stays depleted, or the quad lingers and limits his movement and scrambles, the floor drops back toward the Week 5-6 games.
swingFactors: Return timing from the quadriceps injury
Nelson and Cross back protecting him
Whether the short and screen game stops costing points

confidence.note: He is out with an uncertain return, the line is in flux, and the per-depth splits rest on modest samples.
